guidance.heading: Outlook
section: The information in this section is forward-looking and should be read in conjunction with the section entitled “Additional Information - Cautionary Note Concerning Factors That May Affect Future Results”.

On August 5, 2026, Thomson Reuters provided a full-year 2026 outlook for the company, which included its Global Print business (August 2026 outlook). On November 3, 2026, the company updated its 2026 full-year outlook for the total company to remove and reflect the results of its Global Print business as discontinued operations (November 2026 outlook). As a result, the financial measures presented for the total company in its November 2026 outlook were updated to reflect its expected performance on a continuing operations basis. The company's November 2026 outlook for its "Big 3" segments was unchanged from its August 2026 outlook.

In addition to the updates to reflect the November 2026 full-year outlook on a continuing operations basis, the company also raised its full-year November 2026 outlook for net interest expense to approximately $190 million representing the upper end of the $180 million - $190 million range from the company's August 2026 outlook. The company's updated outlook for net interest expense incorporates the recent debt issuance and the proceeds from the Global Print transaction. We also adjusted our November 2026 outlook for depreciation and amortization of software.

On October 1, 2026, Thomson Reuters completed the sale of a 51% stake in its Global Print business to capital accounts advised by KKR. The two parties formed a joint venture to operate the Global Print business, now operating as Westbridge Print. Beginning October 1, 2026, Westbridge Print will pay a royalty to Thomson Reuters equal to 20% of its Professional revenues (approximately 85% - 90% of its total revenues) for the exclusive license to distribute the company’s intellectual property in print and on ProView, its eBook platform. Additionally, Westbridge Print entered a multi-year agreement whereby it will reimburse us for certain transition services as the joint venture migrates to a stand-alone entity. Beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026, the royalty and transition services reimbursement are largely expected to offset the stranded costs from the separation. Overall, we expect the impact from the Global Print transaction to be approximately neutral to our adjusted EBITDA margin following the transaction close, as well as 60 - 70 basis points accretive to our annual organic revenue growth rate.
